S53.01.note: The Browse button comes from the shared directory panel; the catalogue and detail views are the same screens used for the Installed list.
steps: Open Settings and choose Skills under the Customize group.
Click Browse at the top right of the Skills page.
Look for the catalogue list of skills, including ones not yet installed.
Click one skill name to open its detail page and check it opens.
S53.01.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Browse (then Add from the catalog)

S53.02.note: The list header 'Installed' is the catalogue label for skills; the Status column text comes from the skill data, not a fixed label.
steps: Open Settings and choose Skills under the Customize group.
Look at the list of skills shown for this account.
Check the Status column of each row (for example 'Available' or an installed state).
Compare the rows with the skills you know are active for this account.

labels.text: No skills of your own yet.

S53.03.needs: an account that can create skills
S53.03.note: Creating a skill is shown only when the account has the skill-create capability; the page ownership rule itself is server-side and not visible here.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click Add and choose Create a skill.
Fill in Name, Description and Instructions, then click Create skill.
Check the new skill appears in your own list, and that the empty-state text 'No skills of your own yet.' is gone.
S53.03.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Add > Create a skill

S53.06.note: Instruction text is shown through the Rendered and Raw buttons in the skill file viewer.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click any skill name in the list.
Check the detail page shows the description, the Source and access section, and the skill's instructions (Rendered and Raw buttons).
Check the Enable skill switch and the Try in chat button are visible.

S53.07.note: The manage list columns for skills are name, author and updated date (constants.ts), so the description may show only in the catalogue and detail views; the fallback Skills table in SettingsModal shows description under the name but the web app does not render that fallback.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click Browse and look at the catalogue cards.
Check each skill shows its name and a description line.
Click a skill and check the Description label appears on the detail page.

S53.08.needs: a signed-in account with at least one skill
S53.08.note: The copy 'Use one in chat with / or @' exists only in the fallback Skills panel in packages/ui/ui/src/settings-modal/SettingsModal.tsx, which the web app does not render; the slash menu itself is the visible guidance.
steps: In a chat, click the message box and type /.
Look for the skill names in the menu, each with its description.
Open Settings > Skills, click a skill and find the Try in chat button.
Check that the text tells you how to use the skill (slash name, button, or automatic matching).
S53.08.where: Chat message box > type / (slash), or Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Try in chat

S53.09.needs: an account that can create skills
S53.09.note: The editor dialog title is New skill for create mode; an edit entry point for an existing own skill was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click Add and choose Create a skill.
In the dialog, find the Instructions field and type or edit text.
Click Create skill (or Save changes when editing) and check the text is kept.
S53.09.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Add > Create a skill (editor dialog titled New skill)

S53.10.note: The UI shows the bundled files; whether the model reads them during a run is not visible in the Skills screens.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click a skill that has more than one file.
Look at the Skill files list and click a reference file.
Check the file content appears, with Copy file contents and Download file available.
S53.10.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Skill files

S53.11.needs: a skill with a script file and code execution allowed
S53.11.note: No control runs scripts directly; execution happens inside the chat tool loop and is inferred from the chat output.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills, click a skill whose Skill files list includes script files.
Start a chat, select that skill with Try in chat, and send a request that needs the script.
Look in the chat for a code run or tool result that the skill's script produced.
S53.11.where: Effect appears in chat, when a skill that bundles scripts runs code; the script files are listed under Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Skill files

S53.14.needs: a skill that declares required tools
S53.14.note: The slash menu line is built from the tool list (skillRequirementNote); the label text is 'Needs' followed by the tool names.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click a skill that declares tools.
Find the Needs tools row on the detail page and read the tool names.
Open the chat slash menu (type /) and check the same skill shows a Needs line with those tools.
S53.14.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Needs tools

S53.15.needs: a skill that declares connectors, and a connector account
S53.15.note: Enforcement at run time is server-side and not visible on the page.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click a skill that needs connectors.
Find the Needs connectors row and read the connector names.
Check each connector shows a connected state, or an option to open it when it is not connected.
S53.15.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Needs connectors

S53.17.needs: a signed-in account with at least one skill
S53.17.note: Whether the reply actually uses the skill is a judgement for the tester, not checked by the code reference.
steps: In a chat, click the Add attachments and tools button next to the message box.
Click Skills and choose a skill name from the list.
Check the Skills entry now shows the chosen skill name in place of Skills.
Send a message and check the reply follows that skill.
S53.17.where: Chat > Add attachments and tools > Skills > [skill name]

S53.18.needs: a skill with a clear description and an account that has it installed
S53.18.note: Matching happens on the server when no skill is selected; the UI shows no indicator of it, so the tester can only judge from the reply.
steps: Start a new chat without choosing any skill from Add attachments and tools.
Send a request that matches the description of a skill you have installed.
Look at the reply for the skill's style or steps, without any skill name shown in the message box.
S53.18.where: Effect appears in the chat reply, with no skill chosen; no UI control selects it

S53.20.needs: an installed skill that is not your own (own skills have no switch on the detail page)
S53.20.note: The switch shows only for installed, non-editable skills (SkillDetailView.tsx); the list switch appears when the row has an enabled state.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills, and click an installed skill.
Switch Enable skill off and read the hint text about keeping it in the catalogue.
Check the skill is still listed and its status changes.
Switch Enable skill back on and check the skill is offered again in the chat slash menu.
S53.20.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Enable skill

S53.21.needs: a file to upload (.zip, .skill or SKILL.md)
S53.21.note: The Upload a skill item is added only when the upload capability exists; the editor also has an Import a SKILL.md button.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills.
Click Add and choose Upload a skill.
Pick a .zip, .skill or SKILL.md file from your computer.
Check the skill appears in the list and can be opened and used.
S53.21.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > Add > Upload a skill

S53.22.note: Download works per file; no whole-skill package export was found in the skill screens.
steps: Open Settings, then Skills, and click a skill.
Click a file in the Skill files list.
Click Download file.
Check the file saves to your computer with the same content as shown.
S53.22.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Skill files > [file] > Download file

S53.36.note: Skills have no separate permissions list; the summary shows tools, connectors and source. The Permissions heading exists only for plugins (constants.ts).
steps: Open Settings, then Skills, and click a skill.
Scroll to the Source and access section.
Read the Source row and the Needs tools and Needs connectors rows, plus Added and Version if shown.
Compare the Source text with where you got the skill (built in, uploaded or your own).
S53.36.where: Settings > Customize > Skills > [skill name] > Source and access
